evidence.fact: On August 13, 2015, the Russian Government officially announced the expansion of the food embargo to include Albania, Montenegro, Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Ukraine.
On June 2015, the Russian Government extended the original 2014 food embargo on imports from the US, EU, Canada, Australia, and Norway to remain effective until August 5, 2016.
In 2015, there were no Russian government statements indicating a potential lifting of food sanctions; instead, official statements confirmed the expansion and extension of the embargo.

On July 29, 2015, President Vladimir Putin signed Presidential Decree No. 391, which mandated the destruction of banned products found in the Russian market, reinforcing the strict enforcement of the embargo.
The embargo was initially imposed in August 2014 as a one-year ban and was subsequently extended in 2015 with the possibility of another one-year extension.

reasoning: Based on the evidence, the Russian government explicitly extended the food embargo on the US, EU, Canada, Australia, and Norway until August 5, 2016, in June 2015 [2]. Furthermore, in August 2015, the embargo was expanded to include additional countries like Iceland, Albania, and Montenegro [1]. Official statements from 2015 confirmed the extension and expansion of the ban rather than any intention to lift it [3]. The signing of Presidential Decree No. 391 in July 2015 further solidified the enforcement of the ban by mandating the destruction of banned products [4]. Given the explicit extension to August 5, 2016, and the lack of any statements suggesting a lift prior to that date, it is highly unlikely that Russia would officially lift any part of the embargo before August 6, 2016.
